character.name: Walt Harmon
character.description: Designed from a description: four candidate faces, one pick, then a turnaround sheet and four views. Retired harbour pilot, tall and lean, usually in a navy wool peacoat. Everything that makes him is one .portraius file, face data included. A character made from photos also carries the webcam consent record.

sections.title: Images with an identity score
sections.body: Each still is scored against Walt's own face data, in the browser. 80 or more is a strong match. Under 60, the app retries once on its own and shows both.

sections.title: Make it real
sections.body: One click adds real skin texture to a still, then scores it again. Here the score went from 96 to 81: still a strong match, and the reason the app scores the result instead of assuming it.

sections.title: Video, draft first
sections.body: A clip without people starts as a cheap 480p draft. The 1080p final is rendered from the draft's ID, with nothing sent again. A clip with a person in it renders on MiniMax H3 and is scored one frame a second.

sections.title: Recast
sections.body: Walt takes over a performer's clip, keeping the motion, the timing and the camera. The original performer is a designed person made for testing; Recast only ever takes a face from your vault.

items.caption: Motion Transfer: the dancer's moves, timing and camera, performed by Walt. Drag the line to compare. A full-body dance far from the lens keeps his face small, so it scores low even when it reads as him; waist-up clips score higher.

media.alt: The original and the recast in one 9:16 frame, then the Made with Portraius Studio end card

sections.title: Director
sections.body: A scene planned as shots: film settings once, an anchor still per shot, a clip per shot, then one MP4 joined in the browser with crossfades.

media.alt: The Letter: a retired harbour pilot finds a letter he never sent, in three shots

sections.title: Elements
sections.body: Outfits, props and locations are saved like characters, from 1 to 6 photos, and ride along in any shot: type @ and pick them, like a person.
